title: Hot-reload configuration (IOptionsMonitor in production)
hook: Hot-reload lets your Web API pick up configuration changes without restarting — IOptionsMonitor.OnChange is how singleton services react to feature flag flips and rotated secrets in production.

blocks.text: Hot-reload configuration means the application reads updated settings while running. JSON files with reloadOnChange: true use a file watcher. Azure App Configuration and Key Vault providers poll or receive push notifications. IOptionsMonitor<T> exposes CurrentValue that updates when the underlying IConfiguration change token fires, and OnChange registers callbacks. IOptions and raw environment variables do not reload — only providers that raise change notifications participate.

blocks.text: Restarting pods to flip a feature flag causes connection drains and slow rollouts. Hot-reload enables gradual feature exposure, emergency kill switches, and log level changes without redeploy. In Kubernetes, editing a mounted ConfigMap does not always propagate to running pods instantly — understand provider-specific behavior. Senior interviews ask how IOptionsMonitor works in singleton services, thread safety of OnChange handlers, and when reload is inappropriate (schema changes, connection pool URL changes).

blocks.title: Not everything should hot-reload
blocks.body: Feature flags and log levels — yes. Database connection string changes — usually require restart because connection pools cache the old server. Document which settings are reload-safe.

sequenceDiagram
  participant File as appsettings.json

  Svc->>Svc: update volatile flags

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Expecting IOptions to reload. Heavy work in OnChange blocking the change callback thread. Not using volatile or locks when multiple threads read cached options. Hot-reloading connection strings without recycling DbContext pool. Assuming K8s ConfigMap edits instantly update mounted files — propagation delay varies.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: toggle feature flag in Azure App Configuration sentinel, measure time-to-effect via structured log 'FeatureFlagsReloaded' and compare to pod restart approach. dotnet-trace if OnChange handler blocks — watch thread-pool queue length. For IOptionsMonitor feature flags in API gateways, ensure all pods receive reload within SLA or use external flag service (LaunchDarkly) for cross-process consistency. Document reload-safe settings in runbooks. OpenTelemetry: span attribute on first request after flag flip.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Saying all configuration hot-reloads including env vars. Not knowing IOptionsMonitor is required for singleton hot-reload. Claiming DbContext connection string can change live without restart. Unable to explain thread safety of OnChange callbacks.

interviewTakeaways: Hot-reload requires providers with change tokens (JSON reloadOnChange, Key Vault, App Configuration) plus IOptionsMonitor.
IOptions never reloads; IOptionsSnapshot refreshes per request; IOptionsMonitor.OnChange updates singletons.
Production tip: use IOptionsMonitor for feature flags; restart pods for connection string changes.
60s: reloadOnChange watches JSON. Change token fires. IOptionsMonitor recomputes and calls OnChange. Singleton services subscribe. Env vars don't reload. DbContext URL needs restart.
Follow-up: how does Azure App Configuration sentinel key pattern work for selective refresh?
commonPitfalls: Saying 'change appsettings and IOptions updates' gets you rejected — IOptions is cached for app lifetime.
Blocking OnChange with network I/O — delays all configuration reload callbacks.
Strong answer: 'IOptionsMonitor with OnChange for singleton feature flags. volatile cache. JSON reloadOnChange locally. App Configuration in Azure. Restart for connection pools.'
introducedIn: reloadOnChange in ASP.NET Core 1.0; IOptionsMonitor.OnChange in 2.0

jsTsCorrelations.concept: nodemon process restart vs in-process reload
jsTsCorrelations.note: Node dev workflow often restarts the whole process on file change. ASP.NET Core reloads configuration in-process via change tokens — no process restart for flag flips.
NestJS can watch .env files with limited support. ASP.NET Core's IOptionsMonitor is the production-grade pattern for singleton services reacting to config pushes.
